title: Post-call: regional cost delta & token economics (FinServe pilot)
text:
Post-call: regional cost delta & token economics (FinServe pilot)

['From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Luca Bianchi <luca@finserve.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@finserve.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: regional cost delta & token economics (FinServe pilot)

Hi Luca / Marta — thanks again for the 30-min sync today. Short recap + next steps so we all have the same frame for the pilot and pricing follow-up.

Key points from call:
- Pilot scope: 3-month proof-of-value for our customer-facing summarization model (chat+generation endpoints).
- Expected volumes: pilot 20M tokens/month, growth plan to 150–250M tokens/month in Q2/Q3 if engagement metrics look good.
- Target budget band (customer indicated): $1k–$6k/month for pilot; realistic scale budget TBD.

Questions we agreed to confirm by EOD: token unit economics target ($/1M tokens), regional cost delta (US vs EU), and any data-residency premium. I ran a quick model during the call — attaching a simple workbook and a short regional summary.

Quick, high-level guidance (ballpark, non-binding):
- Baseline unit: US standard hosted region: $/1M tokens = $50–$70 (volume discounts at commit).
- EU hosted region: ~15–22% premium vs US for identical service (driven by infra egress, region pricing, and multi-AZ operational footprint).
- Data-residency (customer-managed VPC / Private deployment) adds ~10–15% on top of regional price due to isolated capacity and audit retention requirements.

Examples on your stated pilot volumes:
- Pilot (20M tokens/mo) at US-list $60/1M => ~$1,200/mo; EU route at +20% => ~$1,440/mo.
- Scale (200M tokens/mo) with committed discounts might bring unit down into the $30–$45/1M range depending on reserved capacity.

Attachments: estimate_token_costs.xlsx (spreadsheet with scenarios), regional-pricing-summary.pdf (short note), SOC2-snapshot.pdf (requested checklist).

Next steps / asks:
1) Luca / Marta: confirm expected sustained volume after pilot (range is fine).
2) Redwood (Karthik / Rishi): prepare two proposals — a) Hosted US primary; b) EU primary + data-residency option. Include 3-month pilot pricing and a 12-month reserved estimate.
3) Agree on pilot success criteria (accuracy / latency / cost per inference).

I can have an initial draft proposal by COB tomorrow if you can confirm the post-pilot volume range (low/likely/high).

Thanks — Tessa
-- 
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: regional cost delta & token economics (FinServe pilot)

Tessa — thanks, helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volumes: pilot = 20M/mo (for initial 3 months). If pilot meets KPIs, we expect a stepped ramp: month 4–6 -> 60–80M/mo, month 7+ -> 150–220M/mo.

2) Budget: pilot budget ceiling is firm at $6k/mo; ideal pilot target is ~$2k/mo. We understand enterprise pilots sometimes need flexibility — please indicate the minimum footprint to operate within $6k.

3) Residency: regulatory asks require EU data residency for EU customers. For the pilot, EU resident data only applies to EU-based customers (small subset) — that will be ~25% of pilot traffic. If we move forward to private deployment later, that will likely be all EU traffic.

Specific asks for your proposal: 
- Concrete US vs EU $/1M numbers for the three volume bands we discussed (pilot 20M, mid 60–80M, scale 150–220M).
- Explicit line for data-residency add-on and what it buys (VPC, KMS integration, audit logs retention).
- Any minimum commitments needed to hit the lower unit price bands.

Also attached a short internal note summarizing compliance needs for EU customers (I can share if useful).

Thanks — Luca

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: regional cost delta & token economics (FinServe pilot)

Luca — great, thanks for the clarifications. Based on your volume bands and budget constraints, below is a concrete starting structure we can model into a formal proposal. I’ll have a draft by EOD tomorrow and will pull legal/pricing for committed tiers.

Proposed quick-model (non-binding):
- Pilot (20M/mo): US hosted list: $60/1M => $1,200/mo. To meet your $6k ceiling we can include extra burst capacity and a 25% pilot discount (intro) to come to ~$900/mo.
- Mid ramp (60–80M/mo): target $/1M = $45–$50 with a 3–6 month commit. Example: 75M @ $48 => $3,600/mo.
- Scale (150–220M/mo, reserved): target $/1M = $28–$38 with 12-month reserved capacity. Example: 200M @ $32 => $6,400/mo.

Regional and residency deltas (applied multiplicatively):
- EU-hosted premium: +18% on top of the US base (covers infra and ops).
- Data-residency / Private deployment premium: additional +12% (isolated pools, KMS/HSM, longer retention).

Illustrative math for your pilot (20M):
- US baseline (no residency): $60/1M -> $1,200/mo (before any pilot discount).
- EU-hosted (25% of traffic residency during pilot): blended = 0.75*$60 + 0.25*(1.18*$60) = $61.8 average per 1M -> ~$1,236/mo.
- If pilot discount applied (25% intro): blended -> ~$927/mo.

What I’ll include in the draft proposal tomorrow:
- Line items for US vs EU hosted pricing per volume band.
- Explicit data-residency add-on with descriptions of what is included (VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, retention SLA, SOC2 evidence).
- Commitment breakpoints and example economics for 3- and 12-month reserved options.
- A one-page pilot contract (simple SOW + success criteria).

Immediate asks from you to finalize draft:
- Confirm the pilot makeup: % EU traffic (you said ~25% — confirm yes/no).
- If there are any hard constraints on latency for EU users (we can choose smaller region footprint but that can affect cost).

Karthik / Rishi — I’ll need a quick sanity check on the percent deltas above and whether we can approve a 25% pilot discount for the account to get the trial into their $6k budget.

Thanks — Tessa
